bib.title: A Survey of Frontiers in LLM Reasoning: Inference Scaling, Learning to Reason, and Agentic Systems

question: How can LLM reasoning research be organised along regimes (inference scaling vs learning to reason) and architectures (standalone LLM, single-agent, multi-agent)?
contributions: A taxonomy along two orthogonal dimensions, regimes and architectures, each viewed through input (prompt, perception, communication) and output (candidates, action, coordination) perspectives
A comparison of learning algorithms (SFT, PPO, REINFORCE/RLOO, GRPO, DPO) and of training reasoners and verifiers (ORM, PRM, generative)
Identified trends (inference scaling to learning to reason; standalone to agentic) and open challenges (evaluation, understanding reasoning, data)

limits: Survey reports no experiments of its own; every number is relayed from cited work and should be cited to that work
Excludes reasoning benchmarks (footnote 1) and defers domain-specific logic/maths depth to other surveys
Multi-agent coverage is thin on LLM-specific work: Sec 5.3 leans on MARL papers (Matta 2019, Zhang 2021, Ruan 2022) and few LLM multi-agent training papers
Coverage cut around early 2025 (Figure 1 to 2/2025, v4 dated 17 Mar 2026); DeepSeek-R1, o1, Deep Research, Manus are the newest systems named
Authors concede unresolved: whether agentic reasoning always helps on simple tasks, lack of proactiveness, faithfulness of CoT, evaluating reasoning beyond outcomes, scarcity of verifiable data
practices: Use verifiers (oracle where ground truth exists, else ORM/PRM/generative) to select or refine actions; PRMs generally help more than ORMs at inference (Sec 3.2.1)
Do not rely on self-refinement without a robust verifier; several studies show poor results (Sec 3.2.1)
Guard against reward hacking of verifiers and over-refinement in critic loops (Sec 2.3.3)
Choose centralized communication for efficient resource allocation but accept single point of failure; decentralized for no hierarchy (Sec 3.3.1)
Use group-based debate (GroupDebate) to cut token cost while keeping reasoning quality (Sec 3.3.1)
Use confidence-weighted voting for consensus in round-table discussion (ReConcile, Sec 2.3.4)
Prefer step-level or process supervision data from MCTS rollouts when human step labels are too costly, noting poor generalisation beyond the sampling policy (Sec 4.2.2)
Treat learned verifiers as part of the environment when classifying systems (Sec 2.3.2, 5.1.2)
Spend a small curated high-quality dataset rather than large noisy SFT data when a strong base model is available (Sec 5.4.1)

terms.definition: A Reasoner generates the reasoning steps (the policy model); Verifiers evaluate the correctness of the final outcome and/or reasoning steps (reward functions); a Refiner improves reasoning trajectories using verifier feedback
A single LLM, playing one or more components, that operates without interacting with external environments or collaborating with other LLMs
A system with agent-environment interaction (tools, retrieval, verifiers); interactiveness and autonomy mark an agent, with agenticness a spectrum (Kapoor et al. 2024)
A system that additionally incorporates agent-agent communication: N agents, often with distinct roles, and M rounds of message exchange
Divides reasoning into a generator and an evaluator (verifier, compiler) that acts as the environment giving feedback
Divides reasoning into a reasoner, a critic giving feedback, and a refiner that revises flawed actions
Two or more agents debate, then reach consensus via a judge, weighted voting or a fixed number of iterations
Round-table discussion where agents reach consensus through voting or confidence levels, e.g. confidence-weighted voting in ReConcile
Enhancing reasoning at test time by increasing computation before the answer, without updating model parameters
Training models to reason before deployment by simulating inference to generate trajectories and training on them with SFT/RL
Three ways to define the MDP action for RL on LLMs; full response is a one-step MDP as in DeepSeek-R1
Predefined interaction patterns for agent systems (Schluntz & Zhang 2024)
